The students() view accepts POST requests and passes user input (data['name']) directly to Student.create(), which uses unsafe Python string formatting in the SQL query. This is the source for the SQL injection vulnerability in sqli/dao/student.py.

User-controlled review.review_text is rendered in a Jinja2 template without explicit escaping (| e filter). Since autoescape=False is configured globally in sqli/app.py, any HTML or JavaScript in review text will be executed in browsers of users viewing the course.
User-controlled student 'name' is rendered without escaping. Combined with the global autoescape=False setting, this allows stored XSS via student names.

Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False, disabling automatic HTML escaping of template variables. This security misconfiguration enables XSS vulnerabilities across all templates where user input is rendered without explicit | e filters.
The students() view handler allows POST requests to create new students without any authentication check. An unauthenticated attacker can create arbitrary student records.

extra.message: The csrf_middleware is commented out in the application middleware stack. All state-changing POST endpoints (login, logout, student/course creation, reviews, evaluations) are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks because CSRF tokens generated in templates are never validated.

RedisStorage is initialized with httponly=False, meaning session cookies are accessible to client-side JavaScript. Combined with XSS vulnerabilities, this allows session hijacking via malicious scripts.
The 500 error template dumps the entire error.__dict__ object, which may expose sensitive internal information such as exception details, file paths, and configuration data to end users.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The application is initialized with debug=True, which may expose detailed error messages, stack traces, and other sensitive debugging information in production environments.
